text:
Maya S.: Heads up — canary on prod-canary-2 (mixed profile: INT8 baseline + FP8 attention for last layers) is showing a weird 'token stitching' formatting regression and a short hallucination spike for our JSON-table outputs. Repro steps attached below.

Jonathan K.: :eyes: can you paste an example output? and which model variant exactly?

Maya S.: Example output (truncated):
```
{"rows": [{"id": 1, "cells": ["Name", "Age"]}, {"id": 2, "cells": ["Alice", "30"]}, {"id": 3, "cells": ["Bob", "<NOISE>duplicate_cell"]}]}
```
The last row sometimes duplicates a cell fragment from earlier tokens (e.g., `duplicate_cell`) or inserts `\u0000`-like placeholders. Happens only on canary when routing hits the mixed-quant pool. Local gptq-only runs look clean.

Li W.: repro note: we saw this when batch_size=8 and kv-cache enabled. With batch_size=1 it's less frequent. Could be batching + FP8 accumulation edge.

infra-bot: deploy noticed on canary: service/redwood-runtime-prod-canary-2 rolled from sha@b5c4 -> sha@c3a1 (2024-06-18T15:01Z)

Eva R.: Ran eval harness on the canary vs gptq-only baseline:
- JSON-table exact match: baseline 96.2% -> canary 88.9% (drop 7.3pp)
- QA span F1: baseline 92.1 -> canary 90.8 (drop 1.3pp)
- Hallucination rate (schema errors per 1k prompts): baseline 3.4 -> canary 11.2
So biggest delta is structured table outputs.

Samir P.: could be tokenizer alignment when quant noise slightly shifts tokenization boundaries. Did we change tokenizer config or added any new merges?

Maya S.: Not touching tokenizer. But the mixed profile runs FP8 kernels for attention matmul in last two layers — maybe numerical jitter at segment boundaries. We also had a small scheduler change: preference to pack small requests into the same batch for throughput.

Jonathan K.: Quick ideas:
- Re-run the same prompts with deterministic seed and `--disable-batching` to isolate batch effects.
- Run a per-layer FP8 toggle (last-1, last-2) to see if regression localizes.
- Capture raw token ids/responses pre-detokenize.

Li W.: I can run small matrix: (batch=1,4,8) x (kv-cache on/off) x (fp8-layers: none, last-1, last-2, all) and collect token-level diffs. Will post results in ~90m.

Maya S.: attaching a minimal repro script (node snippet) that hits the canary route and logs token ids: 
```
// snippet
const res = await fetch("https://api.redwood.dev/generate", {body: JSON.stringify({model: "redwood-phi-mix-v1", prompt: input})});
console.log(res.tokens); // tokens array
```
Jonathan K.: Ran the script offline against local AWQ-int8 build — couldn't reproduce the duplicate_cell but saw rare `\u0000` nul tokens when batch>4. Might be padding-handling bug in the FP8 kernel.

Eva R.: Also checked eval prompt granularity: if the harness concatenates prompt + instruction differently (newline vs space), the canary is more sensitive. So small prompt formatting changes amplify the effect.

Samir P.: Plan suggestion: 1) patch canary to force batch-size=1 and disable packing, see if metric restores; 2) run per-layer FP8 ablations; 3) if repro is stable, bisect kernel diff between c3a1 and b5c4.

Maya S.: Agreed. I'll push a short-lived override to route canary mixed-profile traffic to a no-packing runtime and flip batch=1. If metrics recover we at least confirm batching interaction.

Li W.: quick update (30m): early matrix shows major deltas only when both `kv-cache=on` AND `fp8` for last-1 layer. With kv-cache off the JSON exact match is +5pp. So KV boundary + quant noise seems plausible.

Jonathan K.: Could be KV cache serialization precision mismatch between FP8 stored cache vs INT8/FP32 expectations. Check cache dtype and encode/decode paths.

tokenizer-bot: Tokenization check completed for sample set. Noted that some prompts produce overlapping subword boundaries: e.g., [`du`, `plicate`, `_cell`]. Overlap frequency ~0.6% of corpus.

Eva R.: If we confirm this is an interaction (kv-cache + fp8-last-layer), recommend rolling the mixed-profile back from prod-canary-2 and re-run controlled experiments. Customer-facing canary shouldn't degrade structured outputs.

Maya S.: Rolling back mixed profile on canary now (will keep a trace). Thanks all — Li can you post the full matrix when done and we'll schedule a short triage sync if needed. :+1:

Li W.: Will post results in thread. If anyone wants immediate logs ping me. :coffee:

Samir P.: If rollback shows immediate improvement let's gate mixed-profile until kernel patch and cache dtype audits are complete. :thinking_face:
